title.en: I used to live in Leeds

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj je bilo in zdaj ni več (I used to live in Leeds, There used to be a shop), zanikaš in vprašaš (didn't use to, Did you use to …?) in veš, kdaj ostane past simple.
goal.de: Du sagst, was früher so war und jetzt nicht mehr ist (I used to live in Leeds, There used to be a shop), verneinst und fragst (didn't use to, Did you use to …?) und weißt, wann das past simple bleibt.
goal.it: Dici ciò che era così e adesso non lo è più (I used to live in Leeds, There used to be a shop), neghi e chiedi (didn't use to, Did you use to …?) e sai quando resta il past simple.
goal.en: You can say what was so and isn't now (I used to live in Leeds, There used to be a shop), say no and ask (didn't use to, Did you use to …?), and know when the past simple stays.

say.sl: **I used to live in Leeds**: **used to** + osnovna oblika za to, kar je bilo in zdaj ni več. (Nekoč sem živel{m:|f:a} v Leedsu.) Za vse osebe je enako: **Mrs Hartley used to live in Leeds.** Slovenščina reče *nekoč* ali *včasih*. **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** (Pri mostu je bila nekoč trgovina.)
say.de: **I used to live in Leeds**: **used to** + Grundform für das, was früher so war und jetzt nicht mehr ist. (Früher habe ich in Leeds gewohnt.) Für alle Personen gleich: **Mrs Hartley used to live in Leeds.** Deutsch sagt *früher*. **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** (Früher gab es bei der Brücke ein Geschäft.)
say.it: **I used to live in Leeds**: **used to** + la forma base per ciò che era così e adesso non lo è più. (Una volta abitavo a Leeds.) Uguale per tutte le persone: **Mrs Hartley used to live in Leeds.** L'italiano usa l'imperfetto. **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** (Una volta c'era un negozio vicino al ponte.)
say.en: **I used to live in Leeds**: **used to** + the base form for what was so and isn't now. The same for every person: **Mrs Hartley used to live in Leeds.** **There used to be a shop by the bridge.**

say.sl: **Old Wilf used to walk to school**: **used to** je za navado, ki je ni več, in za stanje. (Stari Wilf je nekoč hodil v šolo peš.) **Mr Tyson used to count the sheep by hand.** Za used to je vedno osnovna oblika: **walk**, **be**, **have**. Ljudje pišejo tudi *I use to*, slišati je enako; v pisanju je **I used to**.
say.de: **Old Wilf used to walk to school**: **used to** steht für eine Gewohnheit von früher und für einen Zustand. (Der alte Wilf ist früher zu Fuß in die Schule gegangen.) **Mr Tyson used to count the sheep by hand.** Nach used to immer die Grundform: **walk**, **be**, **have**. Man schreibt auch *I use to*, es klingt gleich; geschrieben steht **I used to**.
say.it: **Old Wilf used to walk to school**: **used to** è per un'abitudine di una volta e per uno stato. (Il vecchio Wilf una volta andava a scuola a piedi.) **Mr Tyson used to count the sheep by hand.** Dopo used to sempre la forma base: **walk**, **be**, **have**. Si scrive anche *I use to*, il suono è lo stesso; per iscritto **I used to**.
say.en: **Old Wilf used to walk to school**: **used to** is for a habit that has gone, and for a state. **Mr Tyson used to count the sheep by hand.** After used to, always the base form: **walk**, **be**, **have**. People also write *I use to*, and it sounds the same; writing wants **I used to**.

say.sl: **I didn't use to like tea**: zanikano z **didn't use to**, brez -d. (Včasih nisem maral{m:|f:a} čaja.) Ljudje pišejo tudi *didn't used to*, slišati je enako; v pisanju je **didn't use to**. Pogosto je tudi **never used to**, bolj uradno **used not to**.
say.de: **I didn't use to like tea**: verneint mit **didn't use to**, ohne -d. (Früher habe ich Tee nicht gemocht.) Man schreibt auch *didn't used to*, es klingt gleich; geschrieben steht **didn't use to**. Oft auch **never used to**, förmlicher **used not to**.
say.it: **I didn't use to like tea**: negativo con **didn't use to**, senza -d. (Una volta il tè non mi piaceva.) Si scrive anche *didn't used to*, il suono è lo stesso; per iscritto **didn't use to**. Spesso anche **never used to**, più formale **used not to**.
say.en: **I didn't use to like tea**: no is **didn't use to**, with no -d. People also write *didn't used to*, and it sounds the same; writing wants **didn't use to**. **never used to** is common too, and **used not to** more formal.

say.sl: **Did you use to live here?** Vprašanje z **Did**, spet use brez -d. (Si nekoč živel{m:|f:a} tu?) **Where did you use to work?** (Kje si nekoč delal{m:|f:a}?) Kratek odgovor: **Yes, I did.** **No, I didn't.**
say.de: **Did you use to live here?** Die Frage mit **Did**, wieder use ohne -d. (Hast du früher hier gewohnt?) **Where did you use to work?** (Wo hast du früher gearbeitet?) Kurz geantwortet: **Yes, I did.** **No, I didn't.**
say.it: **Did you use to live here?** La domanda con **Did**, di nuovo use senza -d. (Una volta abitavi qui?) **Where did you use to work?** (Dove lavoravi una volta?) Risposta breve: **Yes, I did.** **No, I didn't.**
say.en: **Did you use to live here?** The question takes **Did**, and again use with no -d. **Where did you use to work?** A short answer: **Yes, I did.** **No, I didn't.**

say.sl: **We went to Keswick last Tuesday**: kdaj, kolikokrat, koliko časa pove past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **used to** pove le, da je bilo tako: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Tudi **We went** je tu prav.) Sedanjika nima: zdaj je **I usually walk**.
say.de: **We went to Keswick last Tuesday**: Wann, wie oft, wie lange sagt das past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **used to** sagt nur, dass es so war: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Auch **We went** stimmt hier.) Eine Gegenwart hat es nicht: jetzt **I usually walk**.
say.it: **We went to Keswick last Tuesday**: quando, quante volte, quanto tempo li dice il past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **used to** dice solo che era così: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Anche **We went** qui è giusto.) Non ha il presente: adesso **I usually walk**.
say.en: **We went to Keswick last Tuesday**: when, how many times and how long take the past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **used to** only says it was so: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (**We went** is right here too.) It has no present: now it's **I usually walk**.

say.sl: **I don't live there any more**: **any more** (ne več) pove, da je mimo. **still** (še) pove, da še traja: **I still walk.** (Še vedno hodim peš.) Skupaj z used to: **I used to smoke, but I don't any more.** (Včasih sem kadil{m:|f:a}, zdaj ne več.) **anymore** se piše tudi skupaj.
say.de: **I don't live there any more**: **any more** (nicht mehr) sagt, dass es vorbei ist. **still** (noch) sagt, dass es noch gilt: **I still walk.** (Ich gehe noch immer zu Fuß.) Zusammen mit used to: **I used to smoke, but I don't any more.** (Früher habe ich geraucht, jetzt nicht mehr.) **anymore** schreibt man auch zusammen.
say.it: **I don't live there any more**: **any more** (non più) dice che è finito. **still** (ancora) dice che dura: **I still walk.** (Vado ancora a piedi.) Insieme a used to: **I used to smoke, but I don't any more.** (Una volta fumavo, adesso non più.) **anymore** si scrive anche attaccato.
say.en: **I don't live there any more**: **any more** says it's over. **still** says it isn't: **I still walk.** With used to: **I used to smoke, but I don't any more.** **anymore** is also written as one word.

exercises.text: — When I was a boy, there ___ (be) a school by the beck. We ___ (walk) there every day, even in the snow. — ___ you use to like it? — No! I ___ (not like) the teacher. After school we ___ (help) in the mill: Mr Tyson's father ___ (have) it then. — Was there a bus? — A bus! There ___ (not be) any buses, you know.

translation.sl: — Ko sem bil deček, je bila ob potoku šola. Tja smo hodili peš vsak dan, tudi v snegu. — Vam je bilo tam všeč? — Ne! Učitelja nisem maral. Po šoli smo pomagali v mlinu: takrat ga je imel oče gospoda Tysona. — Je vozil avtobus? — Avtobus! Avtobusov takrat ni bilo, veš.
translation.de: — Als ich ein Bub war, gab es beim Bach eine Schule. Wir sind jeden Tag zu Fuß hingegangen, auch im Schnee. — Sind Sie gern hingegangen? — Nein! Den Lehrer habe ich nicht gemocht. Nach der Schule haben wir in der Mühle geholfen: Damals hatte sie der Vater von Mr Tyson. — Gab es einen Bus? — Einen Bus! Busse gab es keine, weißt du.
translation.it: — Quando ero bambino, c'era una scuola vicino al ruscello. Ci andavamo a piedi ogni giorno, anche con la neve. — Le piaceva? — No! Il maestro non mi piaceva. Dopo la scuola aiutavamo al mulino: allora era del padre di Mr Tyson. — C'era un autobus? — Un autobus! Di autobus non ce n'erano, sai.
translation.en: — When I was a boy, there used to be a school by the beck. We used to walk there every day, even in the snow. — Did you use to like it? — No! I didn't use to like the teacher. After school we used to help in the mill: Mr Tyson's father used to have it then. — Was there a bus? — A bus! There didn't use to be any buses, you know.

translation.it: Da giovane nonna Maggie ballava ogni sabato. Alla Packhorse Inn c'era un ballo. Il violino non le piaceva, ma Arthur lo suonava. — Ballava anche Lei, Arthur? — No, io suonavo tutta la notte!
translation.en: Granny Maggie used to dance every Saturday when she was young. There used to be a dance at the Packhorse Inn. She didn't use to like the fiddle, but Arthur played it. — Did you use to dance, Arthur? — No, I used to play all night!
